{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 1990 | image = | dates = 13 May – 2 September 1990 | teams = 15 | connacht = | munster = Cork | leinster = Offaly | ulster = Antrim | matches = 14 | poty = [[File: Colours of Cork.svg|border|20px]] [[Tony O'Sullivan]] | team = Cork | titles = 27th | captain = [[Tomás Mulcahy]] | manager = [[Michael O'Brien (hurling manager)|Michael O'Brien]] | team2 = Galway | captain2 = [[Joe Cooney]] | manager2 = [[Cyril Farrell]] | totalgoals = 63 (4.5 per game) | totalpoints = 395 (28.21 per game) | topscorer = [[File: Colours of Cork.svg|border|20px]] [[John Fitzgibbon (Cork hurler)|John Fitzgibbon]] (7-09) | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1989|1989]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1991|1991]] }} The '''1990 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 104th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter county|inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. The draw for the 1990 provincial fixtures took place in November 1989. The championship began on 13 May 1990 and ended on 2 September 1990. [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] were the [[1989 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]] but were defeated by [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the Munster final.{{cite news|url=https://www.the42.ie/jim-nelson-antrim-hurling-1980792-Mar2015/|title=The man who famously led Antrim to 1989 All-Ireland final has passed away|publisher=The 42|access-date=3 March 2018|date=9 March 2015}}{{cite news|url=https://www.the42.ie/tipp-cork-great-moments-1621354-Aug2014/|title=Tipp v Cork: 7 classic moments from one of hurling's great rivalries|publisher=The 42|access-date=3 March 2018|date=15 August 2014}} [[London GAA|London]] qualified for the championship for the first time in two years. On 2 September 1990, Cork won the championship following a 5–15 to 2–21 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the All-Ireland final.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/classic-final-1990-cork-5-15-galway-2-21-129678.html|title=Classic final: 1990: Cork 5–15 Galway 2–21|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=25 July 2015|date=3 September 2010|first=Jim|last=O'Sullivan}} This was their 27th All-Ireland title, their first in four championship seasons. Cork's [[John Fitzgibbon (Cork hurler)|John Fitzgibbon]] was the championship's top scorer with 7-09. Cork's [[Tony O'Sullivan]] was the unanimous choice for [[Texaco Hurler of the Year|Hurler of the Year]]. ==Championship draw== As a result of the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] [[Association football|football]] team qualifying for the [[1990 FIFA World Cup]], the [[Munster GAA|Munster Council]] took precautions in avoiding a fixtures clash and a potential loss of revenue by changing the dates and times of their games. == Team changes == === To Championship === Promoted from the [[All-Ireland Senior B Hurling Championship]] * London (qualified) === From Championship === Regraded to the [[All-Ireland Senior B Hurling Championship]] * Derry * Kildare * Westmeath ==Teams== ===Overview=== A total of fifteen teams contested the championship, two fewer teams than participated in the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1989|1989 championship]]. The [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster championship]] was reduced to five teams as [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] decided to opt out and field a team in the [[All-Ireland Senior B Hurling Championship]]. The [[Ulster Senior Hurling Championship|Ulster championship]] was reduced to just two teams as [[Derry GAA|Derry]] also decided to field a team in the lower championship. === General information === Fifteen counties will compete in the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]: one team from the [[Connacht Senior Hurling Championship]], five teams in the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]], six teams in the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]], two teams from the [[Ulster Senior Hurling Championship]] and one team from the [[All-Ireland Senior B Hurling Championship]].
